query: How do I repot a houseplant?
answer:
The best time to repot is in spring. Signs a plant needs it include roots growing out of the drainage holes or over the soil, soil that dries out very fast, and slow growth even when you fertilize [1].

1. **Pick a pot.** Go no more than about 2 inches (5 cm) wider than the current pot, and make sure it has drainage holes. Clean a reused pot with 1 part bleach to 9 parts water and rinse it well. Don't put gravel in the bottom, because that actually makes drainage worse [1].
2. **Prepare the soil.** Use fresh potting mix, not garden soil, and moisten it before you start [1].
3. **Get the plant out.** Turn the pot upside down with your hand spread over the soil and tap the rim on a table edge until the plant slides out. Don't pull it by the stem [1].
4. **Loosen the roots.** If roots are circling the root ball, cut or unwind them. Trim off any mushy or dead roots.
5. **Replant.** Put some mix in the new pot so the top of the root ball sits about an inch below the rim. Fill in around the sides and firm the soil gently without packing it. Don't bury the plant deeper than it was before [1].
6. **Water.** Water thoroughly until it drains out the bottom [1]. For a week or two afterward, keep the plant in bright, indirect light and hold off on fertilizer while it recovers.

sources.title: How to Repot a Houseplant – NC State Extension, Wayne County
